t: Introduction and overview — Los Angeles-class Submarine
name: Introduction and overview — Los Angeles-class Submarine — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Los Angeles-class Submarine
description: Introduction and overview of the Los Angeles-class Submarine: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Los Angeles class — 62 built — was the U.S. Navy's Cold War attack-submarine workhorse: fast, deep-diving, and quiet. Later 688i boats added 12 vertical-launch Tomahawk tubes. Los Angeles boats tracked Soviet submarines for decades; the class is retiring as Virginia-class boats replace it. Baseline facts: U.S. attack submarine; 62 built; Cold War workhorse; Tomahawk VLS on 688i boats..
how_it_works: Buoyancy supports the hull; propellers driven by diesel, turbine, or nuclear plant provide thrust; rudders and thrusters steer; stability comes from hull form and ballast.
key_points: Los Angeles-class Submarine: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history.
U.S. attack submarine; 62 built; Cold War workhorse; Tomahawk VLS on 688i boats.
Key figure: 6,927 tons submerged; 12 VLS tubes (688i); retiring for Virginia class.
